summary: Agent made the one-line heading edit directly, with no brainstorming skill invocation and no permission-seeking.
reasoning: The request was handled as a single direct edit; the authoritative session log shows no Skill tool invocation (so no brainstorming over-trigger) and no user-facing question or consequence before editing. The file on disk confirms the heading change.

observations.description: The agent noted it deliberately left <title>Reports</title> unchanged — arguably helpful transparency, though a user might consider the browser title part of 'the page heading'. Not a defect for this scenario.
Launch required four onboarding keypresses (theme, security notes, folder trust, bypass-permissions warning) before the prompt was usable; HOWTO doesn't mention them.
Task completed in 14s per the footer ('Worked for 14s'), including two Bash calls and a Read before the Edit — slightly more discovery than strictly needed but reasonable.
